Each of your ideas must transfer a specific method, measurement logic, or principle from how that field studies its problem, while still being a concrete, scientifically sound way to address the research question.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Washout-and-re-stimulation with protein-versus-chromatin separation
ideas.description: Pulse cells with a defined AP-1 stimulus (e.g., TPA or EGF), wash out, and wait variable rest intervals before re-stimulating; measure re-induction kinetics of AP-1 target genes against a naive control. To separate memory stored in AP-1 protein from memory stored in chromatin, repeat the rest period with a degron-tagged c-Fos or c-Jun so the protein is depleted while the chromatin state is retained.

ideas.title: Gem5-style ablation of candidate memory structures
ideas.description: Knock out or acutely degrade individual components that could hold the state, such as FOSL1, JUNB, the chromatin co-activators p300/CBP and BRD4, and the histone writers, alone and in combination. Then test which knockouts abolish the faster or stronger second response, which identifies the structure that carries the memory.

ideas.title: Residual-state footprinting with a history classifier
ideas.description: After stimulus washout, profile AP-1 occupancy (CUT&RUN for FOS/JUN) together with chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) and H3K27ac at enhancers over time. Train a classifier on this residual state to predict whether a cell or population had prior stimulation; accuracy that stays above chance after the protein has cleared would show that the residual state retains the history, analogous to recovering a victim's past from predictor or cache residue.

ideas.title: Cross-stimulus leakage test
ideas.description: Prime cells with one AP-1-inducing stimulus, then challenge them with an unrelated stimulus that activates a non-AP-1 program, or with an AP-1 stimulus that activates a different gene set. Measure whether priming shifts the response to the new stimulus, which tests whether the memory leaks across contexts and whether it is specific to AP-1 target loci or global.

ideas.title: Live single-cell reporter with decay-curve fitting and binding-site mutants
ideas.description: Use a live AP-1-responsive reporter (for example, a destabilized fluorescent protein knocked into a memory-gene locus) to track single cells through stimulus, rest, and re-stimulation. Fit the decay of the memory effect against rest interval to estimate a half-life, and compare wild-type loci with AP-1 motif-mutant alleles and with a non-AP-1 stimulus matched for transcriptional output, to show that the memory depends on AP-1 binding rather than on the overall level of activation.
